# ui::PathSegment

Header: `winui/render/PathGeometry.hpp`.

One piece of a figure, starting where the previous one ended. A [`Line`](../controls/shapes.md#uiline) uses [`p1`](#p1) as its end point; a `Quadratic` has one control point [`p1`](#p1) and ends at [`p2`](#p2); a `Cubic` has control points [`p1`](#p1) and [`p2`](#p2) and ends at [`p3`](#p3).

Arcs never appear here: the [PathGeometry](path-geometry.md) builders and [PathGeometry::parse()](path-geometry.md#parse) convert them to cubics.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::PathFigure figure{.start = ui::Point{0, 0}};
figure.segments.push_back({.kind = ui::PathSegmentKind::Line, .p1 = ui::Point{10, 0}});
figure.segments.push_back({.kind = ui::PathSegmentKind::Quadratic,
                           .p1   = ui::Point{15, 5},
                           .p2   = ui::Point{10, 10}});
```

## kind

```cpp
PathSegmentKind kind = PathSegmentKind::Line
```

The segment type; decides which points are read.

## p1

```cpp
Point p1 {}
```

The end point of a [Line](../controls/shapes.md#uiline), else the first control point.

## p2

```cpp
Point p2 {}
```

The end of a Quadratic, the second control point of a Cubic.

## p3

```cpp
Point p3 {}
```

The end of a Cubic; unused otherwise.

## end

```cpp
Point end() const
```

The point the segment ends at, whichever member that is for its [`kind`](#kind).
